description: A secured SvGrid Studio screen. SvAuthGate requires a signed-in user before it shows the grid, presenting a login and sign-up form and a signed-in bar with sign out. The demo uses a mock auth client so any email and password works with no backend; in a real app you pass your supabase-js client through createSupabaseAuth, and Row-Level Security scopes each user to their own rows: auth establishes who, RLS enforces what.

faq.question: What does SvAuthGate render?
faq.answer: A login form with a sign-up switch while there is no session, and its children plus a signed-in bar once there is one. Sign out clears the session and returns to the form.

faq.question: How do I connect Supabase Auth?
faq.answer: Create your client with createClient(url, anonKey) and pass it through createSupabaseAuth as the gate's client. Sessions persist in the browser, so a reload keeps the user signed in.

faq.question: Does signing in restrict the data?
faq.answer: Not by itself. Authentication identifies the user; Row-Level Security policies on the table use that identity to decide which rows the data source can read and write.
